title: Conducting and engineering Staton's New York sessions
summary: McRae took charge of the date with Hank Jones, Jonah Jones and Jimmy Cleveland, with head arrangements put together in minutes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Now whatever Van was -- I don't think -- Van worked on the coast, because Van didn't come to New York. He was in California. He was writing pictures out there.
See, they only started the album on the coast. But the really -- the things that really -- really that took off for them, he wanted --
He says, 'Since we gonna do Broadway, I'm going to New York and come on, Dakota, we go to

New York, we'll finish it in New York."
Now these are all different type of musicians, because whatchacallem was there. Jonah Jones was on trumpet and the trombone player.
Jimmy Cleveland.
Jimmy Cleveland. Milt Hinton and all those guys.
Eddie Shafnawey on the scene with drums.
Yeah.
Eddie Costa -- I think he was vibes.
Yeah. These men were put all together in New York.
And when we walked in, because they say, "Well, who's conducting the date?" Because they didn't know.
I walked in and I say, "Well I am," you know. And Dave came in, you know. And Dave went on in the control room. He say, "You got it."
"You got it, Teddy, take it," you know. So we started on "You Showed Me The Way"
first. Then we put a head arrangement on that. All these guys -- man, you got five and six guys there -- eight guys there, man.

They could put something together -- especially with Hank. Hank would run the thing down and say, "Hey, we gonna do so and so. We'll put this in-the background," you know. Put a little Basie behind it or a little thing there. Don't steal too much. Don't put too much, (inaudible), because you be running and you get sued, you know. We just be stealing for those ideas and things like that.
And finally, you know, we got a big arrangement. We got an airtight thing together. Now "Broadway", they killed "Broadway". They just went to --

We ran it down two or three times. They was ready to make it. Made the introduction -- what we was gonna make in the introduction, what they gonna do in the background, who's gonna have different solos, what Dakota was going to do.
First time -- I think the third tape that was it. They ran it down with her once, you know.
